subject: literature
passage: Tomasz had met his grandfather perhaps six times, always in the same stiff parlor, and had known him chiefly as a silence at the end of the table. So he was unprepared, when he came to the town after the funeral to help clear the house, for the way it recognized him. The woman at the bakery looked up and said his grandfather's name before she caught herself. The old man at the hardware shop asked whether he still took his coffee black, laughed at his own mistake, and then said, more quietly, that it was the way Tomasz stood in the doorway, one shoulder against the frame. By the third day Tomasz had begun to notice the habit in himself, and he could not have said whether he had always had it or whether he had, somewhere between the bakery and the hardware shop, decided to keep it.
stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.A: Through strangers' recognition, Tomasz discovers a likeness to his grandfather that he begins, perhaps deliberately, to make his own.
choices.B: Tomasz is annoyed that the people of the town keep confusing him with a grandfather he barely knew.
choices.C: The townspeople mistake Tomasz for his grandfather because of the way he stands in doorways.
choices.D: Tomasz resolves to rid himself of the mannerisms that remind the townspeople of his grandfather.

explanation.why: The text opens with how little Tomasz knew his grandfather and then shows the town "recognizing" the old man in him. The last sentence is the key: Tomasz notices the habit "in himself" and cannot say whether he always had it or has "decided to keep it." The main idea joins the strangers' recognition with Tomasz's half-conscious choice to hold on to the likeness.
explanation.A: Correct. This covers both the recognition by strangers and Tomasz's possible decision to keep what they saw in him.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The text gives no sign of annoyance; he is "unprepared" and then begins to adopt the habit.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The doorway is one explanation offered by one shopkeeper; it is a detail, not the point of the text.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This reverses the ending, in which he may have "decided to keep" the mannerism.
